info.title: hausfold.co
info.summary: Public endpoints for hausfold's Mac software: installers, release metadata, docs search, a versioned REST surface, and an MCP endpoint for coding agents.
info.description:
Everything here is public. No API keys, no accounts, nothing to buy. hausfold makes Mac software: haus, a layer that rebuilds a whole Mac from one text file, and small apps that run on it (and without it). See https://hausfold.co/developers/ for prose examples and the MCP tool list.

Versioning and deprecation policy: /v1 is path-versioned. A deprecated endpoint keeps answering and adds a 'Deprecation: true' header plus a 'Sunset' header carrying the date it stops, announced before the date. The un-versioned endpoints (installers, /api/release/{app}, /download/{app}, /api/search, /mcp, /ask, /design.md, the llms.txt files) are the long-lived surface and do not carry a version, because they have never changed shape.

Authentication: none. There is no OAuth authorization server behind this host; see https://hausfold.co/auth.md for the full account of how agents authenticate (they don't). Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json with a machine-readable 'code' field. Rate limiting is per client IP and per edge node, so treat the RateLimit headers as an approximation.

post.summary: Run several read operations in one request
post.description: Takes an array of operations (search, release, install) and answers with one result per operation, in order. Per-operation failures come back as ok:false entries, not as a failed request. For more than 20 operations, use POST /v1/jobs. Supports the Idempotency-Key header: the first response is remembered for 24h and a retry with the same key is answered from memory with Idempotency-Replayed: true.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A client-chosen token (letters, digits, dots, underscores, hyphens; at most 200 characters). The response to the first request carrying this key is reused for every retry with the same key for 24 hours, so a network retry cannot double-apply work.

200.description: One result per operation, in order.

Idempotency-Replayed.description: true when this response was served from the Idempotency-Key memory rather than re-executed.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: What is left of the current window.

post.summary: Run a batch of operations asynchronously
post.description: Same body as POST /v1/batch, but answered immediately with 202 and a Location to poll. The job result is kept for an hour.

202.description: The job was queued. Poll the Location (also given in the body as 'url'); a Retry-After of one second suggests the first poll.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: What is left of the current window.

get.description: Returns the job's current status ('queued' or 'done'; 'failed' only if the job itself crashed) and, once done, its result: one entry per operation, the same shape POST /v1/batch would have answered synchronously.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The job id from the 202 response.

200.description: The job's status, with the result once done.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: What is left of the current window.

get.summary: Natural-language query over the documentation (NLWeb shape)
get.description: One endpoint to ask this site a question: it answers with ranked doc excerpts under '_meta' plus 'results', the NLWeb response shape. Add streaming=true (or an Accept: text/event-stream) for SSE with start, result and complete events. This is docs search, not a chat model.

parameters.name: streaming
parameters.description: true switches the response to text/event-stream (SSE).

200.description: Search results under the NLWeb envelope, or an SSE stream when streaming was requested.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: What is left of the current window.

post.summary: Natural-language query over the documentation, body form
post.description: Same as GET /ask with the query in the body. Set prefer.streaming (or send Accept: text/event-stream) for the SSE form.

200.description: Search results under the NLWeb envelope, or an SSE stream when streaming was requested.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: What is left of the current window.

get.summary: Install script for the haus layer; asks which desktop to build
get.description: Proxies haus's bootstrap.sh with nothing pinned, so the installer interviews you. Run it with `curl -fsSL https://hausfold.co/haus.sh | bash`.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Pin the bootstrap.sh source to an exact haus release tag (vYYYY.MM.DD or vYYYY.MM.DD-N). Unpublished: main is the default.

200.description: The installer as plain text, pinned via HAUS_DESKTOP. `x-hausfold-ref` names the ref it was fetched from.

x-hausfold-ref.description: The ref the script was proxied from (a release tag, or main before the first release).

400.description: A ref that is not a release tag was requested.

502.description: The upstream script could not be fetched.

get.summary: Install script for the hacker desktop, pinned by URL
get.description: Same script as /haus.sh with the hacker desktop pinned, so the installer does not ask. `x-hausfold-desktop` echoes the pin.

get.summary: Install script for the everyday desktop, pinned by URL
get.description: Same shape as /hacker.sh for the everyday desktop.

400.description: A ref that is not a release tag was requested.

502.description: The upstream script could not be fetched.

get.summary: Install script for the minimal desktop, pinned by URL
get.description: Same shape as /hacker.sh for the minimal desktop.

400.description: A ref that is not a release tag was requested.

502.description: The upstream script could not be fetched.

get.summary: Redirect to the latest macOS release artifact of an app
get.description: 302 to the most-preferred macOS asset of the app's latest GitHub release (DMG preferred over the archive). GitHub keeps hosting the bytes and counting downloads.

302.description: Redirect to the asset's download URL, or to the repo's releases page when no signed artifact is found.

404.description: The app slug is not one of the downloadable apps. A non-HTML request is answered with a real 404 whose body is markdown naming where to look (llms.txt, the docs, openapi.json); a browser gets the site's usual 404 page.

get.summary: Latest release metadata for an app (un-versioned alias of /v1/releases/{app})
get.description: The long-lived form of the same document /v1/releases/{app} serves. Kept because it shipped first and is in print.

get.summary: The family's visual standard as one public markdown URL
get.description: Proxied from the workshop repo's docs/design.md. Intended for a coding agent to load before drawing something that carries the brand.

502.description: The upstream file could not be fetched.

get.summary: How agents authenticate (they don't), per the auth.md convention
get.description: Markdown. States the one supported method (anonymous), and what this host deliberately does not implement (no OAuth authorization server, no identity assertions). See https://github.com/workos/auth.md for the convention.

get.summary: The full-text search index of the documentation
get.description: The complete search index (Orama JSON format) behind /docs: one entry per page section with url, breadcrumbs and content. search_docs on /mcp and GET /v1/search both score this same index.

get.summary: Documentation as markdown for LLMs, index form
get.description: One entry per docs page. Plain text, no runtime.

get.summary: Documentation as markdown for LLMs, full text
get.description: Every docs page's full text in one file. Plain text, no runtime.
Generated from the same tool table /mcp serves, so the two cannot drift. Lets an agent preview the server before opening a transport connection.

post.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP. Stateless: no session ids, and GET is refused (405) because there is nothing to stream. Open CORS, no authentication. Initialize, then list or call tools; every tool reads public data. Responses carry the RateLimit trio.

parameters.name: mcp-protocol-version
parameters.description: Optional. Informational for this server: negotiation happens in the initialize request's protocolVersion parameter; the response's mcp-protocol-version header names the version the server answered with.

200.description: JSON-RPC response (single object, or array for a batch).

RateLimit-Remaining.description: What is left of the current window.

202.description: The request (or every message in the batch) was a notification; there is nothing to reply.

405.description: Method not POST. GET would open an SSE stream; this server has nothing to push.

options.description: Open preflight: any origin, POST, and the MCP headers.

installer.description: The installer as plain text, pinned via HAUS_DESKTOP. `x-hausfold-ref` names the ref it was fetched from and `x-hausfold-desktop` echoes the pin.

x-hausfold-ref.description: The ref the script was proxied from (a release tag, or main before the first release).

x-hausfold-desktop.description: The desktop this URL pinned. Absent on /haus.sh, which pins nothing.

app.name: app
app.description: An app with signed, notarized macOS releases on GitHub.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: The next_cursor value from the previous page. Omit (or leave empty) for the first page.

problem.description: RFC 9457 problem+json. 'code' is the machine-readable half an agent branches on; 'type' resolves on this host.

code.description: Stable identifier for the failure kind: missing_query, invalid_cursor, unknown_app, unknown_job, invalid_json, invalid_batch, batch_too_large, job_too_large, rate_limited, upstream_unavailable, index_unavailable, method_not_allowed, not_found.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as 'cursor' for the next page; null means this was the last.

pins.description: The desktop this URL pre-answers, or null for /haus.sh, which asks.

data.description: The operation's result when ok is true.

url.description: Where to poll; present on the 202 body.

askResponse.description: The NLWeb envelope: _meta first, then the results.

externalDocs.description: The same surface written for a human, with quickstarts.
